notes.title: CHUCK
notes.summary: The operational intelligence ecosystem: conversation, QBOs, meetings, COE data, automation and reliability.

notes.title: Conversation Intelligence
notes.summary: Natural language, follow-ups, corrections, references and explainability.

notes.title: QBO Intelligence
notes.summary: Meeting + NDA + RFQ truth, analytics, evidence and scoreboards.

notes.title: Meetings & Scheduling
notes.summary: Meeting lookup, confirmation status, reminders and slot planning.

notes.title: Mapping & Admin
notes.summary: Who owns what, organization mappings, protected writes and audit history.

notes.title: Performance & Reliability
notes.summary: Workers, queues, latency, idempotency, diagnostics and safe deployments.

notes.title: COE Reuse & Outreach
notes.summary: Research once, reuse intelligently, then feed outreach evidence back into the database.

notes.title: Data Architecture
notes.summary: D1, Bridge, COE_MASTER, NA databases, indexes, grids and candidate-only reads.

notes.title: COE Cleaner
notes.summary: Turns raw research into usable CALL_DATA / EMAIL_DATA and safely removes known bad or completed leads.

notes.title: Documents / Line Cards
notes.summary: Retrieval support connected to ownership and account context.

notes.title: Scoreboards / Reporting
notes.summary: Weekly and monthly performance views derived from QBO truth.

notes.title: Future / Planned
notes.summary: Planned queue position + ETA and future operational improvements.

notes.title: Rigid Commands
notes.summary: Early commands forced users to repeat full context and exact phrasing.

notes.title: Natural-Language Router
notes.summary: Chuck learned to route normal business questions instead of relying only on rigid commands.

notes.title: Multi-turn Follow-ups
notes.summary: Follow-up operators preserve compatible scope instead of starting every question from zero.

notes.title: “What about Equimin?”
notes.summary: Entity pivots replace only the entity while retaining compatible metrics and period.

notes.title: “And July?”
notes.summary: Temporal pivots replace the period while retaining the selected account or person.

notes.title: Corrections
notes.summary: Phrases like “Cancelled, not No Show” correct stale analytical state instead of broadening it.

notes.title: Pronouns & References
notes.summary: “Who owns them?” and ordinal references resolve against the visible business context.

notes.title: “Where were we?”
notes.summary: Social interruptions no longer destroy the last valid business topic.

notes.title: Conversation State Bloat
notes.summary: Rich multi-turn state could become large, stale or ambiguous if every result was retained blindly.

notes.title: Bounded State + Thread Isolation
notes.summary: State is bounded and Slack roots/threads keep independent context.

notes.title: Explain + Exact Evidence
notes.summary: Users can ask why, show all, more detail, or exact records without rebuilding the question.

notes.title: Human vs Trusted-Agent Output
notes.summary: Human Slack controls hide raw machine payloads while trusted agents retain structured audit capability.

notes.title: Conversation Impact
notes.summary: Less repeated typing, fewer ambiguous follow-ups, and auditable answers with preserved evidence lineage.
notes.impact: Saves human time + reduces query repetition

notes.title: Manual QBO Counting
notes.summary: QBO totals depended on repeated spreadsheet filtering and inconsistent interpretations.

notes.title: Canonical QBO Definition
notes.summary: QBO = Meeting + NDA + RFQ, creating one shared business definition.

notes.title: Approved Meeting Rule
notes.summary: Meeting QBO analytics use approved meeting records rather than every raw form row.

notes.title: Booked vs Actual Date Confusion
notes.summary: Achievement and execution were being mixed when one date field was used for both questions.

notes.title: Separate Date Basis
notes.summary: Booked Date answers QBO achievement; Actual Date answers meeting execution/outcomes.

notes.title: Response ID Identity
notes.summary: Response ID became the strongest identity for a QFR/QBO record.

notes.title: Historical 4-field Fallback
notes.summary: Older rows can fall back to Booked Date + SDR + Actual Date + Prospect Email.

notes.title: Historical Tracker Gap
notes.summary: 1,538 eligible historical records exposed the need to preserve records beyond the current QFR snapshot.

notes.title: QFR → D1 Sync
notes.summary: Explicit qfr refresh UPSERTs Meeting/NDA/RFQ records by text Response ID.

notes.title: D1 Operational Truth
notes.summary: Normal QBO analytics read qbo_records instead of rebuilding the large QFR Truth snapshot.

notes.title: QBO Analytics
notes.summary: Account, SDR, COE, period and subtype analysis run over narrowed D1 candidates.

notes.title: Show-rate Analytics
notes.summary: Meeting outcomes can be summarized as show-rate instead of manually counting outcomes.

notes.title: Ratings Intelligence
notes.summary: SDR/TL rating averages and gaps add quality context beyond pure QBO volume.

notes.title: Weekly / Monthly Scoreboards
notes.summary: Top-3 SDR Crew and COE Crew views automate recurring performance reporting.

notes.title: Reporting Impact
notes.summary: D1-backed analytics remove repeated QFR parsing and manual workbook calculations.
notes.impact: Saves SharePoint calls + manual reporting time

notes.title: Manual Meeting Checks
notes.summary: People repeatedly opened QFR/calendar data to answer basic status questions.

notes.title: Meeting Query Engine
notes.summary: Chuck can find meetings by date, account/client and contextual question.

notes.title: Account + Date + Timezone Filters
notes.summary: Queries can combine account/client filters with dates and timezone-aware presentation.

notes.title: Status Ambiguity
notes.summary: Event, Verdict and reschedule values needed one consistent business interpretation.

notes.title: Canonical Status Engine
notes.summary: Confirmed, Rescheduled, Show, No Show, Cancelled and pending states are normalized deterministically.

notes.title: Tomorrow Meetings
notes.summary: Separate upcoming-meeting view includes CT/IST timing, SDR and APM context.

notes.title: Daily Meeting Confirmations
notes.summary: Full snapshot plus later status-only updates reduce continuous manual checking.

notes.title: Meeting Reminders
notes.summary: Timed reminders surface upcoming calls and confirmation-call needs before the meeting.

notes.title: Scheduling Collisions
notes.summary: Multiple teams/accounts could collide when choosing meeting times manually.

notes.title: Calendar Slot Engine
notes.summary: Chuck models 30-minute availability instead of forcing people to inspect calendars manually.

notes.title: Capacity + Client Rules
notes.summary: Maximum three meetings per slot; one client cannot have two meetings at the same time.

notes.title: Reschedule Reopens Capacity
notes.summary: Rescheduled/declined meetings release capacity instead of blocking stale slots.

notes.title: Meeting Operations Impact
notes.summary: Status, reminders and slots reduce repeated coordination and calendar inspection.
notes.impact: Saves coordination time + reduces scheduling errors

notes.title: Manual Sheet Cleanup
notes.summary: Raw research needed repeated normalization, duplicate checks and channel-specific cleanup.

notes.title: COE Cleaner
notes.summary: Automates the transformation of RAW research into standardized campaign outputs.

notes.title: CALL_DATA + EMAIL_DATA
notes.summary: Outputs are separated so phone and email usability can be handled independently.

notes.title: Owner Review Before Commit
notes.summary: Cleaning and committing data are intentionally separate actions.

notes.title: Bridge.xlsx Runtime Path
notes.summary: The early Cleaner path depended on a SharePoint Excel Bridge and workbook updates.

notes.title: Notify → Then D1
notes.summary: Team notification must succeed before D1 enqueue; retries do not duplicate the Slack post.

notes.title: Upload Lost Session Context
notes.summary: Cleaner command and later file upload could arrive under different Slack root timestamps.

notes.title: Channel + User Session Pointer
notes.summary: Durable Cleaner state follows the requester across unthreaded command/upload transitions.

notes.title: Client-scoped Cleaner
notes.summary: Cleaner can use organization mappings to show only relevant accounts.

notes.title: Removal Gate
notes.summary: Post-generation/pre-Slack gate decides whether known QBO/bad contact data should be removed.

notes.title: QBO Suppression
notes.summary: Existing Meeting/NDA/RFQ prospect emails are removed from reuse where applicable.

notes.title: Email ≠ Phone Usability
notes.summary: Undelivered email removes EMAIL_DATA; unusable phone removes CALL_DATA without automatically killing the other channel.

notes.title: Hash Removal Grid
notes.summary: H00–H63 buckets make repeated removal checks cheap instead of scanning source tables.

notes.title: Cleaner Impact
notes.summary: Less manual spreadsheet cleanup, fewer reused QBO/bad contacts, and fewer large-table reads.

notes.title: Excel Acting Like a Database
notes.summary: Large workbook reads/writes, Office Scripts and SharePoint calls became the limiting architecture.

notes.title: Bridge.xlsx Stage
notes.summary: A smaller Excel staging layer reduced Master interaction but still carried workbook failure modes.

notes.title: Office Script / Table Limits
notes.summary: Operations such as table addRows could fail or move cells, exposing spreadsheet fragility.

notes.title: Move Operational Storage to D1
notes.summary: Database storage replaces repeated workbook mutation for operational processing.

notes.title: bridge_contacts
notes.summary: Reusable researched contacts live in D1 with deterministic bridge IDs and appearances.

notes.title: Appearances Instead of Duplicates
notes.summary: Repeated normalized emails increase appearances instead of creating needless duplicate contacts.

notes.title: coe_workbooks
notes.summary: Workbook/job history is kept separately from contact rows for auditability.

notes.title: COE_MASTER
notes.summary: Canonical reusable contact inventory receives promoted Bridge contacts and newer outreach evidence.

notes.title: NA Databases
notes.summary: Contact_NA_DB, Email_NA_DB and QBO_NA_DB preserve unmatched evidence rather than dropping it.

notes.title: qbo_records
notes.summary: Historical/current Meeting/NDA/RFQ records become persistent operational QBO truth.

notes.title: 300k-row Scan Cost
notes.summary: COE_MASTER was ~301,484 rows, making repeated full scans wasteful.

notes.title: Email Hash / ID Directory
notes.summary: Normalized email hashing narrows lookup directly to candidate records instead of scanning Master.

notes.title: Cleaner Removal Grid
notes.summary: 64 H00–H63 buckets index QBO/undelivered/unusable removal evidence.

notes.title: Candidate-only Reads
notes.summary: Indexes and grids let jobs read only likely rows instead of entire tables.

notes.title: Bridge → COE_MASTER
notes.summary: Promotes reusable Bridge contacts into canonical Master with approved merge rules.

notes.title: Per-row Sync Flags
notes.summary: Marking thousands of Bridge rows synced would create unnecessary write cost and mutation.

notes.title: Cursor-based Daily Sync
notes.summary: One lightweight cursor tracks daily progress; Bridge rows remain reusable and intact.

notes.title: 10k/day · 1k batches
notes.summary: Bridge→Master enforces a 10,000-row daily window and ≤1,000-row batches.

notes.title: Hard Bounce Reconciliation
notes.summary: 17,018 unique valid hard-bounce emails were checked: 11,656 matched COE_MASTER and 5,362 were preserved in Email_NA_DB.
notes.impact: Preserves outreach evidence without full-table rework

notes.title: QBO NA Reconciliation
notes.summary: QBO_NA_DB held 570 unmatched records: 564 were not in COE_MASTER and 6 had no valid prospect email.
notes.impact: Prevents unmatched QBO evidence from being silently lost

notes.title: Data Architecture Impact
notes.summary: Less Excel dependency, fewer scans/writes, reusable research history and bounded database jobs.

notes.title: Research Repeated From Scratch
notes.summary: Previously researched contacts were being rediscovered instead of reused.

notes.title: COE_Reuse
notes.summary: Find usable contacts already in the COE database before starting new research.

notes.title: Already-cleaned Files Reprocessed
notes.summary: Historical cleaned workbooks should not run through the Cleaner and mapping flow again.

notes.title: DB_Upsert
notes.summary: Already-cleaned CALL_DATA can go directly into the D1 append/dedupe pipeline.

notes.title: Outreach_Update
notes.summary: Email/call outreach results are fed back into the canonical contact database.

notes.title: Hard Bounce Evidence
notes.summary: Undelivered email evidence marks the email channel unusable until superseded.

notes.title: Unusable Call Outcomes
notes.summary: Known non-working phone outcomes suppress CALL reuse without automatically suppressing email.

notes.title: Channel Independence
notes.summary: Email and phone usability remain separate signals instead of one all-or-nothing lead state.

notes.title: Old Failure Could Outlive New Evidence
notes.summary: A historical hard bounce or bad outcome must not permanently win over newer positive evidence.

notes.title: Newer Evidence Wins
notes.summary: Delivered can clear older email failure; newer outreach evidence overwrites stale state.

notes.title: Outreach Contact Not in Master
notes.summary: Useful outreach evidence may arrive for contacts that COE_MASTER does not yet contain.

notes.title: Route to NA DBs
notes.summary: Unmatched email/call evidence goes to Email_NA_DB or Contact_NA_DB for later reconciliation.

notes.title: Feedback Loop Into Master
notes.summary: When candidate matches exist, approved outreach fields update canonical Master instead of remaining in isolated files.

notes.title: Reuse + Outreach Impact
notes.summary: Research once, reuse intelligently, and continuously improve contact quality from real outreach.
notes.impact: Saves human research + prevents stale contact evidence

notes.title: Ownership Lived in People’s Heads
notes.summary: Account ownership and reporting relationships were difficult to answer consistently.

notes.title: Organization Mapping
notes.summary: Persistent mappings connect SDR → ATL → Account → COE/APM.

notes.title: Ownership Questions
notes.summary: Chuck can answer who owns/manages an account using the mapping layer.

notes.title: Mappings Change Over Time
notes.summary: A static mapping table is not enough when SDRs/accounts/owners change.

notes.title: Mapping Admin
notes.summary: Authenticated flows add accounts/SDRs, change ownership and activate/deactivate mappings.

notes.title: Slack Identity Resolution
notes.summary: Slack member profiles resolve to canonical human names instead of cryptic owner IDs.

notes.title: Unprotected Mapping Writes
notes.summary: Mapping changes are operationally sensitive and cannot be accepted from arbitrary chat input.

notes.title: Fresh Admin Password Gate
notes.summary: Every D1 mapping write requires a fresh CHUCK_ADMIN_PASSWORD modal submission.

notes.title: Password Never Persisted
notes.summary: Password values are not copied into pending mutation state, queue messages, D1 or audit logs.

notes.title: Mapping Audit Log
notes.summary: Idempotent audit records preserve who changed what and when.

notes.title: Mapping Health / Conflict Checks
notes.summary: Active registered mappings and conflict checks keep hierarchy-derived answers trustworthy.

notes.title: Documents / Line Cards
notes.summary: Account context also helps users retrieve client documents and line cards without hunting folders.

notes.title: Mapping Impact
notes.summary: Ownership becomes queryable, editable under control, and auditable rather than tribal knowledge.
notes.impact: Saves lookup time + reduces ownership errors

notes.title: One Worker Did Everything
notes.summary: Conversation traffic and heavy D1/cleaner jobs competed inside one Worker architecture.

notes.title: Request Pipeline
notes.summary: Slack ingress became lightweight and heavy business work moved through staged queue processing.

notes.title: CPU Isolation
notes.summary: Queues isolate long business stages from the original Slack HTTP acknowledgement.

notes.title: Two-Worker Split
notes.summary: Automation stays focused on Slack/conversation while Data Engine owns heavy COE database work.

notes.title: chuck-automation
notes.summary: Slack ingress, conversation, QBO/meetings, reporting, cleaner review and orchestration.

notes.title: chuck-data-engine
notes.summary: Cleaner database lookups, DB_Upsert, Outreach_Update, COE_Reuse and Bridge→Master.

notes.title: Too Many Queue Hops
notes.summary: PLAN → queue → ANALYZE → queue → PRESENT improved isolation but added visible latency.

notes.title: Latency + Identity Hardening
notes.summary: Reused lifecycle state, parallelized probes and improved canonical owner rendering.

notes.title: Latency Collapse
notes.summary: Normal business requests run PLAN + ANALYZE + PRESENT inside the existing queue consumer.

notes.title: Post-reply waitUntil Work
notes.summary: Provenance and learning bookkeeping move after the visible Slack reply when safe.

notes.title: Immutable Request IDs
notes.summary: One request ID correlates route, analysis, presentation, failure and timing logs.

notes.title: Slack Event Dedupe
notes.summary: Timestamp, actor and thread context prevent reused client_msg_id from suppressing valid messages.

notes.title: Diagnostics + Terminal Failures
notes.summary: Health/version/diagnostic requests must finish with a visible result instead of ACK-only silence.

notes.title: Pause / Resume Operations
notes.summary: Sensitive cleaner/data workflows can be paused around deployments and migrations.

notes.title: Completion Notifications
notes.summary: Long data jobs notify requesters on completion instead of requiring repeated status checks.

notes.title: Bridge Sync Cost Controls
notes.summary: Daily cursor, candidate-only reads and 1,000-row batches keep Bridge→Master bounded.

notes.title: Queue Position + ETA
notes.summary: When capacity is busy, accept the job, show its queue position/estimated start, then notify on completion.

notes.title: Reliability Impact
notes.summary: The system became more responsive under load while preserving idempotency, observability and bounded data work.
notes.impact: Saves Worker CPU + user waiting uncertainty
